title: PR 11 — Vault API: sync, CRUD, trash, folders, authorization
description: Implement the ciphertext-only vault API: incremental sync with tombstones, item create/update/delete/restore/purge, folder CRUD, strict per-user authorization, payload limits, and scheduled purge. Requirement IDs: TASK-29, TASK-30, TASK-31, TASK-32, TASK-33, TASK-34, TASK-35.
acceptanceCriteria: `GET /api/vault?since=<rev>` returns items and folders with `rev > since`, tombstones included, page size capped at 500 with a cursor
Responses contain no plaintext vault fields; only ciphertext, IV, metadata, and rev
`POST /api/vault/items` assigns `rev = ++users.vault_rev` inside a D1 batch and returns the created row
`PATCH /api/vault/items/:id` requires the client's `rev` and returns 409 with the current row on mismatch
`DELETE` soft-deletes, restore clears `deleted_at`, and purge is permanent and idempotent
Folder CRUD works; deleting a folder sets contained items' `folder_id` to NULL and bumps their rev
Every handler scopes by the session `user_id`; foreign ids return 404, never 403
No handler accepts `user_id` from the request body or query
Requests over 256KB return 413 and malformed base64 returns 400
A daily cron purges items deleted more than 30 days ago

steps.details: Create `app/server/vault/rev.server.ts` with `allocateRev(db, userId)` implemented as `UPDATE users SET vault_rev = vault_rev + 1 WHERE id = ? RETURNING vault_rev`. Document that every mutation statement must run in the same `db.batch()` as this allocation so a failed write does not leak a rev.

Create `app/server/vault/sync.server.ts` with `listVaultDelta(db, userId, since, cursor)`, plus `app/routes/api.vault.ts` as a transport-only loader returning `{ serverRev, items, folders, nextCursor? }`. Query `WHERE user_id = ? AND rev > ? ORDER BY rev LIMIT 501`, return 500 rows plus a cursor when truncated, include tombstones with `deleted_at`, and never join or decrypt on the server.

Add `app/server/vault/items.server.ts` use cases for `POST /api/vault/items` and `PATCH /api/vault/items/:id`; the route module stays transport-only. Validate with Zod: type enum, base64 validity, ct ≤ 64KB, iv length, favorite boolean. On update, `WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ? AND rev = ?`; when `meta.changes === 0`, fetch and return 409. Never partially update on validation failure.

Add `DELETE /api/vault/items/:id` (soft), `POST /api/vault/items/:id/restore`, and `POST /api/vault/items/:id/purge`. Purge requires an explicit body flag `confirm: true`. All of them allocate a new rev and return the row.

Add `app/server/vault/folders.server.ts` with list, create, rename, and delete use cases, and `app/routes/api.folders.ts` as a transport-only route. Deleting uses a batch that nulls `folder_id` on contained items, allocates one rev per affected item, and deletes the folder. Validate ciphertext sizes and ownership.

Create `app/server/vault/ownership.server.ts` exporting `requireOwnedItem(db, userId, itemId)` and `requireOwnedFolder(db, userId, folderId)` returning the row or throwing a 404-shaped error. Use them in every mutation path. Add a test that greps handlers for `user_id` sourced from input and fails.

Add a shared `readJson(request, schema, maxBytes=262144)` helper that enforces content length, parses JSON safely, rejects unknown keys, and returns 413/400 as appropriate. Log validation failures with the request id only.

Add a scheduled handler in `workers/app.ts` for `0 3 * * *` that deletes items with `deleted_at < now - 30 days` in batches of 1000 and logs counts only. Document that it runs on the Worker cron trigger.

Vitest: cross-user read/update/delete/restore/purge all return 404; stale rev returns 409 and does not overwrite; sync with `since=serverRev` returns an empty delta; tombstones appear once; oversized payload returns 413; cron purges only expired rows.

technicalNotes: D1 is single-threaded but requests interleave; keep rev allocation and the mutation in one batch.
Never decrypt or inspect ciphertext server-side; the API is a dumb store for opaque blobs.
Return 404 for foreign ids to avoid existence leaks.
Sync must be resumable: the client stores `serverRev` and cursor.
Do not implement conflict merging; the client resolves by refetching.
Route modules under `app/routes/` stay transport-only; vault queries and rules live in `app/server/vault/*.server.ts`.
